entities.name: David J. Baker
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
David Jewett Baker (1792–1869) was an American Democratic politician from Illinois who served briefly as a U.S. Senator (1830) — filling a vacancy for less than two months — and subsequently had a long career as a federal district judge in Illinois (1839–1869). His brief Senate tenure was significant mainly as a biographical footnote, but his thirty-year federal judgeship made him one of the most important figures in the development of Illinois federal law.

Illinois in the 1830s was one of the rapidly growing frontier states of the American West — settled primarily by migrants from the Ohio Valley and Upper South, with a political culture that was strongly Jacksonian Democratic and that produced Abraham Lincoln's early political career in opposition to the Democratic establishment.

Baker's long district court tenure (1839–1869) placed him on the federal bench during the most consequential decades of Illinois history — from the frontier state's rapid development through the Civil War and its aftermath.

He was a foundational figure in Illinois federal jurisprudence.
